title: fix(plugin-form): one `collapsed` / `collapsible` resolution for the default and drawer arms (objectui#9849 step 1)
body:
Part of #9849
Clause-②: no

Step (1) of the two the director ruling orders on this card (comment `5749155880`, letter E, maintainer 「同意」): 「the three `collapsed` / `collapsible` resolutions converge to the declaration-based one objectui#9780 established, before the gate rule lands on it.」 Step (2) (E in `projectSectionDivider`, deleting `SectionDividerGate`, re-pinning `drawerFormSectionDescription-9834` row 5, the diagnostic pin) is ⛔ not in this PR and stays on the card. That is why the first line says `Part of`.

## What changed

- `fieldGroups.ts` gains `resolveSectionCollapse`, beside `projectSectionDivider`. It is module-internal: the package barrel `src/index.tsx` names `fieldGroups` zero times, and `package.json` `exports` declares only `"."`. It is the ONE resolution of the authored pair, and it follows objectui#9780 letter A:
  - `collapsed` implies `collapsible`, read off the declaration and never off the live state.
  - `collapsible: false` with `collapsed: true` resolves to collapsed, with the control present.
  - `collapsible` alone is open, with the control.
  - A section declaring neither member is untouched.
  - A section is only collapsed while it is collapsible, and it is only collapsible when the row the arm draws can carry the control (`hostsControl`). This states the default arm's 「an untitled bucket is never collapsible」 once, for every arm.
- `ObjectForm.tsx` (grouped layout, explicit and derived sections share one loop): the inline objectui#9780 expression moves into the helper. Behaviour is unchanged (see the table).
- `DrawerForm.tsx`, both pushes, now call the same helper:
  - The explicit push was still the objectui#9780 trap: it read `collapsible` alone for the control and `collapsed` unconditionally for the state.
  - The derived push gated the state on `collapsible`, which is a third spelling.
  - The unseeded `useState` replaces a seed that read `collapsed` a second time. An untoggled section falls back to its declaration inside the helper, as in ObjectForm.
- `.changeset/9849-collapse-resolution-converge.md`: `patch` for `@object-ui/plugin-form`.

⛔ No new accepted key or value, no new package export, no new prop. `DrawerFormSectionConfig` and `ModalFormSectionConfig` are unchanged, and no section map in `ObjectForm.tsx` copies a new key.

## Premise, re-measured on `origin/main` `62597c5` by printing every `collaps` line in the four files

- **ObjectForm grouped layout, one site** (the objectui#9780 resolution): `isCollapsible = Boolean(section.collapsible) || Boolean(section.collapsed)`, the state `collapsedSections[key] ?? section.collapsed`, and fields hidden only on `label && isCollapsed`.
- **DrawerForm explicit push**: `collapsible: section.collapsible`, `onToggle` only for `section.collapsible`, and the state `collapsedSections[key] ?? section.collapsed` read unconditionally, which hides the fields. A `useState` seed also read `s.collapsed`.
- **DrawerForm derived push**: the state read only when `section.collapsible`, the control only for `section.collapsible`.
- **ModalForm: zero `collaps` lines.** It has no resolution of its own. Neither route reads either member, `ModalFormSectionConfig` declares neither, and `ObjectForm`'s modal map copies neither. So the modal draws every field and no control, whatever the section declares.
- `fieldGroups.ts` at base only maps the `@objectstack/spec` `collapse` enum onto the pair (`deriveFieldGroupSections`) and copies a resolved pair onto the row (`projectSectionDivider`). Neither step is a resolution.

⇒ The code has **three resolutions, as the ruling says**. objectui#10172, #10161 and #10141 did not move them. But there are only **two in behaviour**:
- The derived drawer push agrees with objectui#9780 on every input an author can write. `deriveFieldGroupLayout` never emits `collapsed` without `collapsible` (the deprecated `collapsed: true` alone maps to `'collapsed'`, which maps to both), and every keyed group gets a heading (label defaults to the key).
- Ablation leg 2 below measures this: putting the derived push back on its old resolution reddens nothing.
- The live trap was the explicit drawer push only.

## Before / after, per route

Read by `__tests__/collapseResolution-9849.test.tsx` through a real renderer. "Before" means the same pin file run against the base source: `Tests 9 failed | 21 passed (30)`. Every failure was on a drawer explicit route or a drawer trap row, and each failed for the right reason (0 controls while the fields were hidden).

| route | `collapsed` alone | `collapsible: false` + `collapsed` | `collapsible` alone | neither | no heading, no blurb, `collapsed` | no heading, blurb, `collapsed` alone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ObjectForm default, explicit `sections` | closed + control → **same** | closed + control → **same** | open + control → same | open, no control → same | open → **same** | open, no control (blurb-only row, objectui#9835 B) → same, not re-pinned here (`objectFormSectionMembers-8071` row 8 owns it) |
| ObjectForm default, derived `fieldGroups` | closed + control → same (both `collapse: 'collapsed'` and deprecated `collapsed: true`) | n/a | open + control → same | open, no control → same | not author-reachable | not author-reachable |
| ObjectForm `formType: 'drawer'` (drawer map) | ⛔ closed, **0 controls** → closed + control | ⛔ closed, **0 controls** → closed + control | same | same | ⛔ fields hidden, **nothing on the page** → open | see next row |
| DrawerForm explicit, direct | ⛔ closed, **0 controls** → closed + control | ⛔ closed, **0 controls** → closed + control | same | same | ⛔ fields hidden, **nothing on the page** → open | ⛔ blurb drawn, fields hidden, **0 controls** → closed, control on the blurb row |
| DrawerForm derived `fieldGroups` | closed + control → same | n/a | same | same | not author-reachable | not author-reachable |
| ModalForm explicit, ObjectForm `formType: 'modal'`, ModalForm derived | every field drawn, no control → **same** (a reading, see below) | same | same | same | same | same |

⚠️ The last column differs between the default arm (open, no control) and the drawer (a control on the blurb row). That is the **gate** residual (`SectionDividerGate`, step 2), ⛔ not the resolution. The default arm's blurb-only row carries no collapse pair under objectui#9835 letter B. The drawer's explicit push draws a row for every member, and `SectionDivider` renders that row when it has a heading or a blurb. Both answers keep the fields reachable, and that is all the new file asserts there.

⚠️ The modal rows are a READING, ⛔ not a ruling. The modal honours neither member, so objectui#9780's one promise (a declared section is never unreachable) holds there trivially. The pin asserts that, and it records "no control" so that step (2)'s 「on every arm」 (ruling E item 1) flips those rows on purpose. Bringing the pair to the modal needs a new member on `ModalFormSectionConfig`, which this step does not add.

## Evidence, all at head `8cb4574b`

**Pins.** New `packages/plugin-form/src/__tests__/collapseResolution-9849.test.tsx`, 30 rows:
- one block per route that emits a collapse pair (3 explicit, 2 derived), each asking the objectui#9780 questions;
- the drawer trap rows;
- the modal reading.

Every zero is lit: each absent-fields row also reads the heading drawn and the same reader non-empty after a click, and each no-control row is paired on its route with a row where the same reader finds one.
- Before, on the base source: `Tests 9 failed | 21 passed (30)`.
- After: 30 passed.

**Ablation.** Run through `ablation-replace.mjs`: each anchor hit exactly once, each write was verified on disk by blob hash and marker count, and each restore was proven by state (blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty) with a wrapper trap on EXIT/INT/TERM. The run covered the new file plus `collapsedImpliesCollapsible-9780`, `objectFormSectionMembers-8071` and `fieldGroupSections.test.tsx` (53 tests). Directions were written down before the run, and all three matched:

| leg | mutation (blob before → during) | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | drawer EXPLICIT push back on its old resolution (`d0dc3ee90d5b` → `c0de0a1cc600`, marker 0 → 3 → 0) | `Tests 9 failed \| 44 passed (53)`: exactly the 9 drawer explicit and drawer trap rows. **Every ObjectForm row stays green**, and so do the #9780 and 8071 files |
| 2 | drawer DERIVED push back on its old resolution (`d0dc3ee90d5b` → `4bda9e2214c5`) | `Tests 53 passed (53)`: predicted, because the old derived resolution is behaviourally identical on every author-reachable input |
| 3 | the ONE helper loses the implication (`c24e82e8e24c` → `8a713103f65a`) | `Tests 10 failed \| 43 passed (53)`: the `collapsed`-alone and contradiction rows on **all three explicit routes at once**, the drawer blurb row, `collapsedImpliesCollapsible-9780` rows 1 and 3, and `objectFormSectionMembers-8071` row 4. One mutation reddens the default arm and the drawer together, which shows that one path serves both |

No `dist/` is involved: the suite imports `plugin-form` from source through the root vitest config, so no dist preflight applies.

**Suites and gates** (heavy runs under the shared verify lock, `VERDICT command-exit 0`):
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/` from the repo root: `Test Files 109 passed (109)`, `Tests 1074 passed | 1 skipped (1075)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form run type-check` echoed `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` and exited 0, after building the dependency closure (`--filter '@object-ui/plugin-form^...' build`, exit 0). `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the new pin file, so its types are checked.
- Lint, as a DECLARED NARROWING to the 4 touched `.ts`/`.tsx` files:
  - population: `eslint.config.js` applies to `**/*.{ts,tsx}`;
  - count: `--format json` reports 4 files, 0 errors;
  - invariance: the config enables no type-aware linting (no `projectService`, no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot move the verdict of a file it does not touch;
  - warnings on the edited sources are unchanged against BASE (ObjectForm 61 → 61, DrawerForm 22 → 22, fieldGroups 0 → 0). The new pin's 13 warnings are all `no-explicit-any` schema casts, the sibling pins' pattern;
  - the repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` (names the changeset), `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers` and `check:vi-mock-override-shape` all exited 0. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over the 5 paths reported NOT GOVERNED. A manual control-byte grep over the 5 files found no match.
- ⚠️ NOT MEASURED locally: the CI farm, including `Spec Main Shape Gate`, which is red on every PR today on untouched test files (objectui#10229). ⛔ Not addressed here.

## Acceptance notes

- **Two edge behaviours moved, both in the safe direction:**
  - Sections that share a key: on the default arm, toggling a collapsible section could hide the fields of a non-collapsible twin whose row had no control. A non-collapsible section is now never collapsed.
  - The drawer no longer seeds its live state at mount, so a section whose declared `collapsed` changes after mount follows its declaration until the user toggles it, as ObjectForm always has.
- `FormSectionContainer` (`FormSection.tsx`, a published React component) has the same pair shape at the prop level. The objectui#9780 report already recorded it as not class (c): it is a component prop, and its only caller (the wizard) passes neither. It is outside this file surface and not touched.
- The pending `.changeset/9849-single-divider-projection.md` says of that change that 「every arm's gate, its collapse resolution and its predicate handling are unchanged」. That was a description of that change's diff, and it is still true of it. This changeset follows it in the same CHANGELOG and states the convergence.
- `check:changeset-claims` asks for a read of `.changeset/8738-object-form-fields-description.md`, which names `ObjectForm.tsx`. It was read: it concerns the top-level `fields` vocabulary, which this diff does not touch, and it is still true.
